title: DevRev Powers Autonomous Support with GPT-6.1 Sol
summary: DevRev deploys GPT-6.1 Sol for Computer and Operator agents, delivering enterprise self-service that balances reasoning speed and cost efficiency.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- DevRev now uses GPT-6.1 Sol to power two autonomous agents, Computer and Operator, for enterprise self-service workflows.
- The implementation balances advanced reasoning capabilities with speed and cost efficiency for production support environments.
- This deployment demonstrates GPT-6.1 Sol's ability to handle complex enterprise tasks while maintaining operational scalability.


DevRev has deployed[GPT-6.1 Sol](https://emergent.sh/news/openai-launches-gpt-6-1-sol-multimodal-ai) to power autonomous self-service capabilities for enterprise customers, marking a significant step forward in production AI applications. The platform uses OpenAI's latest model to run two specialized agents, Computer and Operator, which handle complex support workflows while optimizing for reasoning depth, response speed, and operational costs. Officially launched on November 4, 2026, this implementation showcases how enterprises are moving beyond chatbot interfaces to fully autonomous service systems.


## Computer and Operator Agent Architecture


DevRev's implementation centers on two distinct agents built on GPT-6.1 Sol. The Computer agent handles technical troubleshooting and system diagnostics, navigating complex issue resolution paths that previously required human expertise. The Operator agent focuses on workflow orchestration, managing ticket routing, escalation logic, and cross-functional coordination. Both agents leverage GPT-6.1 Sol's multimodal capabilities to process documentation, code snippets, logs, and user queries simultaneously.


The architecture separates reasoning-intensive tasks from rapid-response interactions. Computer engages GPT-6.1 Sol's extended thinking mode for root cause analysis and multi-step problem solving. Operator uses the model's faster inference paths for classification and routing decisions. This dual-mode approach maintains service quality while controlling compute costs across thousands of daily interactions.


## Balancing Reasoning, Speed, and Cost


DevRev's deployment strategy directly addresses the enterprise AI trilemma of performance, latency, and economics. The team configured GPT-6.1 Sol with dynamic compute allocation, scaling reasoning depth based on query complexity. Simple requests receive sub-second responses using optimized inference, while intricate technical problems trigger deeper analysis with extended token budgets.


Early performance data shows the system handles 78% of tier-one support queries without human intervention. Average resolution time dropped 43% compared to traditional ticketing systems. The cost profile remains competitive with offshore support teams while delivering 24/7 availability and consistent quality. DevRev reports the system maintains accuracy above 92% on factual technical responses, with automatic escalation protocols catching edge cases.


## Release Date and Availability


DevRev officially released this GPT-6.1 Sol-powered system on November 4, 2026, following a six-month beta period with select enterprise customers. The platform is now available to DevRev's existing customer base, with general availability planned for new enterprise clients in Q1 2027. Implementation requires integration with existing ticketing systems and knowledge bases, typically completed within two to four weeks.


## Enterprise AI Production Patterns


This deployment illustrates emerging patterns in enterprise AI adoption. Rather than replacing entire support teams, DevRev positions the agents as force multipliers that handle routine complexity while escalating nuanced cases. The system maintains audit trails for compliance requirements and includes human-in-the-loop checkpoints for sensitive operations.


The choice of GPT-6.1 Sol over alternatives reflects prioritization of reasoning capabilities and multimodal understanding. DevRev engineering teams cite the model's ability to follow complex procedural documentation and maintain context across multi-turn interactions as key differentiators. The platform also benefits from OpenAI's enterprise security features, including data isolation and access controls.


## What This Means


DevRev's production deployment of GPT-6.1 Sol for autonomous service operations demonstrates that enterprise AI has moved beyond experimental pilots into mission-critical workflows. The success of Computer and Operator agents validates the technical feasibility of autonomous support at scale. For enterprises evaluating similar implementations, this case study provides concrete evidence that modern language models can handle the reasoning depth, speed requirements, and cost constraints of production environments. The architecture pattern of specialized agents with dynamic compute allocation may become a template for future enterprise AI deployments across customer service, IT operations, and business process automation.
